nodes.method_thesis: Decompose the allowed unlabeled corpus into a fixed vocabulary of chemically sanitized, attachment-labelled fragments and use its reconstruction trajectories only to behavior-clone a task-agnostic graph policy. In each independent objective session, start complete constructions from a sampled vocabulary fragment and repeatedly sample a three-part categorical action: an open attachment site on the current partial graph, a fragment, and a compatible attachment site on that fragment, with an explicit stop action and valence-checked transitions. Canonicalize completed graphs and submit only fresh valid unique assemblies in the evaluator-announced batch; the vocabulary is a combinatorial action alphabet, not a pool of whole-molecule candidates. Put the scored initial molecules when representable and every subsequently generated trajectory into a task-local replay buffer, assign the observed oracle score only at the terminal transition, and update corrected twin soft-Q critics, the stochastic actor, and its entropy temperature from uniformly replayed transitions. The next molecules are sampled directly from the updated actor, so no corpus molecule is retrieved, ranked, or screened and no finite molecular candidate set is enumerated. Off-policy trajectory reuse lets each scarce terminal observation train many partial-graph decisions, while maximum-entropy action sampling resists early policy collapse; both serve the sole benchmark target of a stronger final Top-1 on each session.

nodes.method_name: ChemTS-style RNN-guided Monte Carlo tree search
nodes.method_thesis: Train a task-agnostic recurrent next-token model on the allowed unlabeled SMILES corpus and freeze it as a chemical-language prior. For each independent objective session, grow a fresh Monte Carlo search tree whose nodes are SMILES prefixes: initialize available path statistics from the ten scored starting molecules, select prefixes by an upper-confidence tree rule, expand them with high-probability unseen tokens from the frozen model, and use model rollouts to complete new molecules. Canonicalize locally and submit batches containing only newly constructed, valid, unique terminal SMILES; after each oracle response, backpropagate the observed scores through the visited prefix paths. The dynamically expanded tree therefore converts 290 feedback calls into increasingly focused de novo construction toward high terminal rewards without updating a policy, fitting a latent surrogate, mutating evaluated parent graphs, or ranking a finite corpus pool.

nodes.method_thesis: Pretrain a task-agnostic autoregressive SMILES model and its sequence representation only on the allowed unlabeled corpus, retain a frozen prior, and restart all task-local state for each independent objective. Fit a probabilistic surrogate only to the ten fixed scored molecules and subsequent oracle-evaluated molecules, while maintaining an oracle-anchor policy updated only from returned true scores. Before each evaluator-announced batch, clone that anchor into a disposable inner policy, optimize the clone without oracle calls using the surrogate posterior mean as its molecular reward, and ancestrally sample a fresh ephemeral set of complete SMILES from the resulting policy. Canonicalize locally, remove invalid, previously evaluated, and duplicate molecules, and select the requested number by greedy batch expected improvement; after feedback, refit the surrogate, update the oracle anchor from the real observations, and discard the inner clone. Thus every submitted molecule is generated de novo, the corpus is never scored or searched as a candidate pool, and surrogate feedback changes the source distribution itself before acquisition rather than merely ranking proposals from a fixed generator. The optimization target is solely the equal-weight mean of the five independent terminal Top-1 scores.

nodes.method_thesis: Train a task-agnostic bidirectional masked discrete-diffusion model on SAFE fragment sequences from the allowed unlabeled corpus, then keep its weights frozen during every objective session. Initialize a dynamic fragment vocabulary only from oracle-evaluated molecules, score each fragment by the observed rewards of molecules containing it, and construct each new starting context by sampling and attaching high-scoring fragments. Replace one complete fragment span with mask tokens and iteratively denoise that span in parallel while conditioning on the retained fragments; canonicalize locally and submit only newly generated valid unique molecules. Oracle feedback updates fragment scores and admits fragments from evaluated offspring, so the generator can repeatedly refine promising chemistry while its learned conditional denoising can synthesize fragments outside the current vocabulary. Every candidate is therefore generated de novo rather than retrieved or ranked from the corpus, and reward-directed fragment regeneration targets improvement of the final Top-1 within the sparse feedback budget.

nodes.method_thesis: Extract a vocabulary of single-attachment fragments from the allowed unlabeled corpus without scoring or retrieving any whole corpus molecule, and start one persistent molecular-graph Markov chain from each of the ten fixed evaluated molecules. In every feedback round, generate one fresh candidate per chain through a locally sanitized, reversible fragment-add or fragment-delete transition, retrying locally until the batch contains ten novel canonical molecules. After the oracle returns, accept each proposed state with a Metropolis-Hastings probability for an annealed score density, including its forward/reverse proposal ratio; rejected proposals leave their chains at the previous states. Low inverse temperature initially permits controlled downhill moves that can cross structural valleys, while increasing concentration later favors high-score states. Thus all oracle calls evaluate de novo molecular constructions, and feedback directly steers persistent search paths toward a stronger final Top-1 without a surrogate, a learned generator, or finite-library screening.

nodes.method_thesis: Learn a task-agnostic forward and backward molecular-construction policy from the allowed unlabeled corpus using an atom-and-fragment graph grammar, then restart that policy independently for each objective. From an empty graph, the forward policy samples chemically valid attachment, bond, and stop actions until it produces a terminal molecule; whole corpus molecules are never retrieved, ranked, or used as a finite candidate pool. After each evaluator-announced batch is scored, map each observed score to a strictly positive tempered terminal reward and train on only oracle-evaluated molecules and their sampled construction/deconstruction trajectories using the trajectory-balance loss, a learned partition function, and reward-prioritized replay. Because trajectory balance assigns terminal probability according to total flow across every construction route rather than merely increasing the likelihood of one elite sequence, online feedback amortizes search into a de novo sampler whose probability mass concentrates on high-reward molecular regions while continuing to expose distinct routes to rare high-scoring structures. The optimization target remains the mean final Top-1 across the five independent sessions; flow statistics and replay usage are mechanism evidence, not substitute objectives.

nodes.method_thesis: Pretrain a task-agnostic autoregressive SMILES model and its sequence representation only on the allowed unlabeled corpus, retain a frozen prior, and restart all task-local state for each independent objective. Fit a probabilistic surrogate only to the ten fixed scored molecules and subsequent oracle-evaluated molecules, while maintaining an oracle-anchor policy updated only from returned true scores. Before each evaluator-announced batch, clone that anchor into a disposable inner policy, optimize the clone without oracle calls using the surrogate posterior mean as its molecular reward, and ancestrally sample a fresh ephemeral set of complete SMILES from the resulting policy. Canonicalize locally, remove invalid, previously evaluated, and duplicate molecules, and select the requested number by greedy batch expected improvement; after feedback, refit the surrogate, update the oracle anchor from the real observations, and discard the inner clone. Thus every submitted molecule is generated de novo, the corpus is never scored or searched as a candidate pool, and surrogate feedback changes the source distribution itself before acquisition rather than merely ranking proposals from a fixed generator. The optimization target is solely the equal-weight mean of the five independent terminal Top-1 scores.

nodes.method_thesis: Train a task-agnostic sequence-to-sequence molecular autoencoder on randomized and canonicalized SMILES views of the allowed unlabeled corpus, then freeze its encoder and decoder. At the start of each independent objective session, encode the ten fixed scored initial molecules as ten persistent particles with latent velocities and personal-best memories. After every oracle response, update the personal and swarm-best memories, move each particle by the Molecular Swarm Optimization rule combining inertia with stochastic attraction toward its own best and the swarm's current and historical best positions, and decode one fresh valid unique molecule from each resulting trajectory for the next announced batch. Oracle scores therefore steer interacting de novo latent trajectories directly, without fitting a surrogate or selecting from the corpus, and the 290 adaptive calls are concentrated on finding an exceptional terminal molecule for final Top-1.
